ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution dominated by low-intensity (black) pixels covering approximately 85% of the surface area, with high-intensity (white) pixels localized primarily in clusters along the trailing edge margins and scattered circular points.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white blobs are localized along the superior margins (trailing edge) of both lobes. The central and inferior regions are characterized by a solid low-intensity black matrix punctuated by small, isolated circular and linear high-intensity white markers.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped central depression with a deep vertical penetration into the fluke body, separating the two lobes symmetrically.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations with high pixel-amplitude; the boundary is characterized by continuous jagged peaks and valleys across the entire superior length of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bi-lateral outward sweep with a concave curvature on the inner margins transitioning to a convex sweep towards the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense distribution of circular and annular high-intensity white pixel clusters (0.5% to 2% of total lobe area each) scattered across both lobes, consistent with localized attachment-site scarring.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple high-contrast linear disruptions; one prominent horizontal white line (~15% lobe width) on the left lobe and several shorter, multi-directional diagonal scratches on the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive rake-mark scarring and circular barnacle-attachment scars distributed across the entire visible ventral surface; irregular trailing edge suggests significant micro-trauma or cumulative tissue wear.
other_distinctive_markers: A large, irregularly shaped white patch is visible on the inner trailing edge of the right lobe, adjacent to the median notch.
